nodes.name: Governing NLS equation with inverse-square potential
nodes.statement: i\partial_t u + \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u &= 0, \quad u(0,\cdot)=u_0\in H^1(\rn),
nodes.label: inls

nodes.name: Hardy's inequality
nodes.statement: c_*\intrn \frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx \le \intrn |\nabla u|^2 dx, \quad u\in H^1(\rn).
nodes.label: hardy

nodes.name: Mass conservation
nodes.statement: \Vert u(t)\Vert_{L^2_x} \equiv \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2_x},
nodes.label: mass

nodes.name: Energy conservation
nodes.statement: E(u(t))=\frac12 \intrn|\nabla u(t,x)|^2\diff x - \frac{c}{2}\int_{\rn}\frac{|u(t,x)|^2}{|x|^2}dx - \frac{1}{p+1}\intrn|u(t,x)|^{p+1}\diff x \equiv E(u_0).
nodes.label: energy

nodes.name: Equivalence of $H$ and the Dirichlet seminorm
nodes.statement: \left(1-\frac{c}{c_*}\right) \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx\le H(u)\le \int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx.
nodes.statement_short: Hardy's inequality makes $H$ comparable to $\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2$.
nodes.label: hardy2

nodes.name: Stationary equation for standing waves
nodes.statement: \Delta\ffi + \frac{c}{|x|^2}\ffi - \ffi + |\ffi|^{\frac{4}{N}}\ffi=0.
nodes.label: sinls

nodes.name: Sharp mass threshold condition
nodes.statement: \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs},
nodes.label: sharp

nodes.name: Lower bound on the energy via $H$
nodes.statement: E(u)\ge \frac12 H(u) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right), \quad u\in H^1(\rn),
nodes.statement_short: Energy controls $H(u)$ once the $L^2$ norm is below the ground-state mass.
nodes.label: posE

nodes.name: A priori bound on $H(u(t))$ below the mass threshold
nodes.statement: H(u(t)) \le 2E(u_0) \left(1-\left(\frac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}\right)^\frac{4}{N}\right)^{-1},
nodes.statement_short: Subcritical mass gives a uniform-in-time bound on $H(u(t))$.
nodes.label: subcritical

nodes.name: Minimal mass blow-up solution family $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ (introduced)
nodes.statement: S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right).
nodes.label: S1.def

nodes.statement: N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0.

nodes.statement: S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right),

nodes.statement: \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}, \quad 0<\limsup_{n\in\N}H(v_n)<+\infty, \quad \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}E(v_n)\le 0.
nodes.statement_short: Mass converging to $M_\mathrm{gs}$, bounded $H$, and non-positive limsup energy.

nodes.name: $H^1$ compactness conclusion
nodes.statement: \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0.
nodes.label: compact

nodes.name: Strong $L^q$ convergence of the translated sequence
nodes.statement: \wt{v}_{n_k} \rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\rn), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*),

nodes.name: Non-vanishing lower bound assumption (contradiction hypothesis)
nodes.statement: \liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R}\frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta.

nodes.name: Lower bound transferred to the cutoff $u_k$

nodes.name: Local well-posedness for the inverse-square NLS
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$. For any initial value $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$, there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$. Moreover, the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$. Finally, if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
conclusions: there exists $T\in(0,+\infty]$ and a maximal solution $u\in C^0_t H^1_x ([0,T)\x\rn)$ of \eqref{inls}, satisfying \eqref{mass}--\eqref{energy} for all $t\in(0,T)$.
Moreover, the blow-up alternative holds: if $T<+\infty$ then $\lim_{t\uparrow T} \Vert \nabla u(t)\Vert_{L^2}=+\infty$.
Finally, if $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N}$, then the solution is global.
nodes.statement_short: Local solutions exist, obey the blow-up alternative, and are global below the $L^2$-critical power.
nodes.label: local.thm

nodes.name: Sharp global well-posedness criterion
nodes.statement: Let $c\in(0,c_*)$ and $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$. If $u_0\in H^1(\rn)$ satisfies \begin{equation} \Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}, \end {equation} then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
conclusions: then the corresponding solution of \eqref{inls} given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm} is global.
nodes.statement_short: Mass strictly below the ground-state mass $M_\mathrm{gs}$ forces global existence.
nodes.label: global.thm

nodes.name: Classification of minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$. Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t). \]
assumptions: Let $T>0$ and $u\in C\big([0,T),H^1(\rn)\big)$ be a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} with $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, which blows up at time $T$, \emph{i.e.}~$\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u(t))=+\infty$.
conclusions: Then there exist a ground state $Q\in \mathcal{G}$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, $u(t)=S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)$.
nodes.statement_short: Every finite-time blow-up solution at the minimal mass is a pseudo-conformal transform of a ground state.
nodes.label: main.thm

nodes.name: Minimization problem and the ground-state equation
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$, \[ \alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u) \] is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler--Lagrange equation \begin{equation} N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta Q +c\frac{Q}{|x|^2}\Big)-\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\right)Q+Q^p=0. \end{equation} Furthermore, \begin{equation} \alpha_{p,N}=2\frac{\|Q\|_{L^2}^{p-1}}{p+1}. \end{equation} In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: $\alpha_{p,N} := \inf_{u\in H^1(\rn)\backslash\{0\}} J^{p,N}(u)$ is attained at a positive radial function $Q\in H^1(\rn)$, solution of the Euler-Lagrange equation \eqref{EL}.
In the case $p=1+\frac4N$, any minimizer of $J^{p,N}$ can be rescaled into a solution of \eqref{sinls}.
nodes.statement_short: The Weinstein-functional minimum is attained at a positive radial solution of the Euler-Lagrange equation, with explicit value, and rescales into a ground state when $p=1+4/N$.
nodes.label: minimization.prop

nodes.name: Existence of explicit minimal mass blow-up solutions
nodes.statement: For all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $T\in\R$, $\lambda_0>0$ and $\gamma_0\in\R$, the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by \begin{equation} S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\frac{\lambda_0^2}{T-t}} e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}} \left(\frac{\lambda_0}{T-t}\right)^{N/2}Q\left( \frac{\lambda_0x}{T-t} \right), \end{equation} is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t} \quad \text{as } t\to T, \] for some $C>0$.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
conclusions: the function $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$, defined by \eqref{S2.def}, is a minimal mass solution of~\eqref{inls} defined on $(-\infty,T)$, and which blows up with speed $\Vert\nabla S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{T-t}$ as $t\to T$, for some $C>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Applying scaling, phase and the pseudo-conformal transform to any ground state gives a minimal mass blow-up solution with speed ~C/(T-t).
nodes.label: blow-up_sol.prop

nodes.name: Variational characterization of ground states
nodes.statement: Let $v\in H^1(\rn)$ be such that \begin{equation} \|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs} \quad \text{and} \quad E(v)=0. \end{equation} Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
conclusions: Then there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, and $\gamma_0 \in \R$ such that $v(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x)$, where $\disp\lambda_0=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(|v|)}}{M_\mathrm{gs}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Any $v$ with minimal mass and zero energy is a ground state up to phase and $L^2$-scaling.
nodes.label: charact.prop

nodes.name: Compactness up to translation at the minimal mass threshold
nodes.statement: Consider a sequence $\{v_n\}_{n\in\nat}\subset H^1(\rn)$ satisfying \begin{equation} \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}, \quad 0<\limsup_{n\in\N}H(v_n)<+\infty, \quad \limsup_{n\rightarrow\infty}E(v_n)\le 0. \end{equation} Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in\nat}$, $\gamma_0\in\R$ and $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \begin{equation} \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\|v_{n_k}-e^{i\gamma_0}Q\|_{H^1}=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A sequence approaching minimal mass with non-positive limsup energy has a subsequence converging strongly, up to translation and phase, to a ground state.
nodes.label: compact.prop

nodes.name: Pseudo-conformal transformation preserves solutions and mass
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}. Then, for all $T\in\R$, the function \[ u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
assumptions: Let $u$ be a global solution of \eqref{inls}.
conclusions: the function $u_T(t,x)=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2}}u\left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right)$ is a solution of \eqref{inls} on $(-\infty, T)$, with $\|u_T\|_{L^2}=\|u\|_{L^2}$.
nodes.statement_short: The pseudo-conformal transform of a global solution is again a solution of the same mass.
nodes.label: pseudo-conf.lem

nodes.name: Concentration-compactness lemma
nodes.statement:
Let $\{v_n\}_{n\in \N}\subset H^1(n)$ satisfy \[ \lim_{n ightarrow\infty}\|v_n\|_{L^2}=M<+\infty \quad 	ext{and} \quad \sup_{n\in\N} H(v_n) <+\infty. \] Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \N}$ that satisfies one of the following properties. \medskip 
oindent (V) $\|v_{n_k}\|_{L^q}ightarrow 0$ as $kightarrow\infty$ for all $q\in(2,2^*)$. \medskip 
oindent (D) There are sequences ${w_k},{z_k}\in H^1(n)$ and a constant $\alpha\in (0,1)$ such that:  egin{enumerate} \item $\dist(\supp(w_k),\supp(z_k))ightarrow\infty$; \item $|v_k|+|z_k|\le |v_{n_k}|$; \item $\sup_{k\in\N} (\|w_k\|_{H^1}+\|z_k\|_{H^1})<+\infty$; \item $\|w_k\|_{L^2}ightarrow\alpha M$ and $\|z_k\|_{L^2}	o (1-\alpha)M$ as $kightarrow\infty$; \item $\lim_{kightarrow\infty} ig| \int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^q-\int_{n}|w_k|^q-\int_{n}|z_k|^q ig|=0$ for all $q\in[2,2^*)$; \item $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty} ig\{ H(v_{n_k})-H(w_k)-H(z_k)  ig\}\ge 0$. \end{enumerate} \medskip 
oindent (C) There exists $v\in H^1(n)$ and a sequence $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset n$ such that \[ v_{n_k}(\cdot -y_k)ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(n), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*). \]
conclusions: Then there exists a subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}_{k\in \N}$ that satisfies one of the vanishing (V), dichotomy (D), or compactness (C) properties.
nodes.statement_short: A bounded-energy sequence either vanishes in $L^q$, splits into two divergent profiles, or compactifies after translation.
nodes.label: conc-comp.lemma

nodes.name: Virial identities for the inverse-square NLS
nodes.statement: Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} on $[0,T)$, such that $u(t)\in \Sigma$ for all $t\in [0,T)$. Then for all $t\in[0,T)$ the following identities hold: \begin{equation} \Gamma'(t)=4\im\int_{\rn} \overline{u}(t,x)(\nabla u(t,x)\cdot x)dx \end{equation} and \begin{equation} \Gamma''(t)=16E(u)+\frac{4}{p+1}(N-Np+4)\int_{\rn} |u(t,x)|^{p+1}dx. \end{equation}
assumptions: Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} on $[0,T)$, such that $u(t)\in \Sigma$ for all $t\in [0,T)$.
conclusions: Then for all $t\in[0,T)$ the identities \eqref{virialone} and \eqref{virialtwo} hold.
nodes.statement_short: The first and second time-derivatives of the radial-moment functional $\Gamma(t)$, in terms of $E(u)$ and the $L^{p+1}$ norm.
nodes.label: virial.lemma

nodes.label: banica.lem

nodes.name: Sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequality (corollary)
nodes.statement: For $1<p<1+\frac{4}{N-2}$ and $u\in H^1(\rn)$, we have \begin{equation} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}, \end{equation} where \[ \alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}} \quad\text{in the critical case} \quad p=1+\frac{4}{N}. \]
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
conclusions: we have $\Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1} \le \alpha_{p,N}^{-1} H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N} \Vert u\Vert_{L^{2}}^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}$, where $\alpha_{p,N}=\frac{M_\mathrm{gs}^{\frac{4}{N}}}{1+\frac{2}{N}}$ in the critical case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$.
nodes.statement_short: The sharp GN inequality follows directly from the minimization result, with $\alpha_{p,N}$ expressed via $M_\mathrm{gs}$ in the critical case.
nodes.label: GN.cor

nodes.name: Symmetries of the inverse-square NLS equation
nodes.statement: More precisely, if $u(t,x)$ solves~\eqref{inls}, then so do: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)] \item $u_{t_0}(t,x)=u(t-t_0,x)$, for all $t_0\in\R$ (time translation invariance); \item $u_{\gamma_0}(t,x)=e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$, for all $\gamma_0\in\R$ (phase invariance); \item $u_{\lambda_0}(t,x)=\lambda_0^{2/(p-1)}u(\lambda_0^2t,\lambda_0x)$, for all $\lambda_0>0$ (scaling invariance). \end{enumerate} Note that \eqref{inls} with $c>0$ is not invariant under space translations and Galilean transformations. The symmetries (a) and (b) are obvious and give rise, via Noether's theorem, to the invariance of the energy and the mass, respectively. The scaling invariance is described in more detail below.

nodes.name: Hardy functional $H(u)$
nodes.statement: For our analysis it is convenient to introduce the {\em Hardy functional}, defined on $H^1(\rn)$ by \[ H(u)=\int_{\rn} |\nabla u|^2dx -c\int_{\rn}\frac{|u|^2}{|x|^2}dx. \]

nodes.name: $L^2$-critical scaling
nodes.statement: p=1+\frac{4}{N}$ yields $2/(p-1)=N/2$ and, as in the classical case $c=0$, \eqref{inls} is invariant under the {\em $L^2$ scaling} \[ u(t,x) \to u_\lambda(t,x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda^2 t, \lambda x) \quad (\lambda>0). \] This transformation preserves the $L^2$ norm and \eqref{inls} is called {\em $L^2$ critical}.

nodes.name: Uniqueness of positive radial solutions of the stationary equation for $c>0$
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, for $c>0$, we are not aware of any uniqueness result for \eqref{sinls} on $\rn$. Uniqueness results for radial solutions of nonlinear elliptic PDEs are typically based on an intricate analysis of the corresponding ODEs in the radial variable $r=|x|$, see {\it e.g.}~\cite{kwong,coffman,peletier,yanagida}. We shall not consider this problem here.
nodes.statement_short: Whether the stationary equation's positive radial solution is unique for $c>0$ is open; not addressed here.

nodes.name: Local well-posedness and uniqueness at the threshold $c=c_*$
nodes.statement: However, it is not clear to us that local well-posedness holds in this case. Trachanas and Zographopoulos \cite[Theorem~3.1]{greeks} claim that (in the radial case) it follows by adapting a proof by Cazenave, but we were not able to carry this through. Let us briefly explain why. For $c\in(0,c_*)$, Theorem~\ref{local.thm} above was proved in \cite{suzuki}, by adapting to $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$ Cazenave's proof of \cite[Theorems~3.3.9]{cazenave}, originally developed to deal with $-\Delta$ in bounded domains, where dispersive estimates are not available. This approach allows one to obtain existence of local (in time) solutions \cite[Theorems~3.3.5]{cazenave}, but an additional uniqueness result is required to obtain the full well-posedness result \cite[Theorems~3.3.9]{cazenave}. In \cite{suzuki}, uniqueness relies on the Strichartz estimates for $-\Delta-c|x|^{-2}$, which were established in \cite{burq}. Unfortunately, as pointed out on p.~521 of \cite{burq}, these estimates break down at the threshold value $c=c_*$. Hence, the existence of local in time solutions is ensured by \cite{suzuki}, but it is not clear if and how uniqueness can be proved. As uniqueness is essential in our proof of Theorem~\ref{main.thm}, we shall only consider $c\in(0,c_*)$ here. Note that, for $c=c_*$, inequality \eqref{crucial} also breaks down, and we do not know how to prove the crucial Proposition~\ref{compact.prop}.
nodes.statement_short: Whether local well-posedness (hence the classification) extends to $c=c_*$ is unresolved.

nodes.name: Self-similar profile of the minimal mass blow-up family
nodes.statement: Note that these solutions present a self-similar profile, in the sense that, for all $t\in [0,T)$, there exists $\lam(t)>0$ such that $|S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x)|=\lam(t)^{N/2}Q(\lam(t)x)$. Hence, up to a time-dependent $L^2$ rescaling, $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ keeps the same shape as $Q$ while blowing up.

nodes.name: Weinstein functional $J^{p,N}$
nodes.statement: Consider the Weinstein functional \[ J^{p,N}(u):=\frac{H(u)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|u\|^{2+\frac{p-1}{2}(2-N)}_{L^2}}{\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}. \]
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Consequences of the Euler-Lagrange characterization
nodes.statement:
oindent (a) Note that, by phase invariance of $J^{p,N}$, if $u$ is a minimizer so is $e^{i	heta}u, \ 	heta\in\R$. \medskip 
oindent (b) For $p=1+ rac{4}{N}$, the Pohozaev identity for \eqref{sinls} implies that any minimizer $u$ of $J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}$ satisfies $E(u)=0$, that is \[ H(u)= rac{1}{1+ rac{2}{N}}\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}, \] and so  egin{equation} J^{1+ rac{4}{N},N}(u) = rac{H(u)\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{\|u\|_{L^{2+ rac{4}{N}}}^{2+ rac{4}{N}}} = rac{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}^{ rac{4}{N}}}{1+ rac{2}{N}}. \end{equation} Therefore, all minimizers have the same mass. \medskip 
oindent (c) The proof of Proposition~ef{charact.prop} below shows that all minimizers are positive and radial, up to a global phase factor.
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: gs_scaling.rem

nodes.name: $L^2$-scaling of ground states
nodes.statement: The $L^2$ scaling $u_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}u(\lambda{x})$ yields \[ H(u_\lambda)=\lambda^2H(u), \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}, \quad \Vert u_\lambda\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}=\lambda^2 \Vert u\Vert_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}, \quad \text{hence} \quad J^{p,N}(u_\lambda)=J^{p,N}(u). \] Therefore, if $Q$ is a ground state, then $Q_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x)$ is again a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, satisfying $\Vert Q_\lambda\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and the rescaled Euler--Lagrange equation \[ \Delta Q_\lambda+ \frac{c}{|x|^2}Q_\lambda-\lambda^{2} Q_\lambda + |Q_\lambda|^{\frac{4}{N}}Q_\lambda=0. \] It follows from Remark~\ref{minmass.rem} below that the ground states are the solutions of \eqref{sinls} with smallest mass.
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
nodes.label: scaling.rem

nodes.name: Ground states have the smallest mass among standing waves
nodes.statement: It follows from Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} that any solution $\ffi$ of \eqref{sinls} satisfies $\|\ffi\|_{L^2}\ge M_\mathrm{gs}$. Otherwise, applying Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} with $u(t,x)=e^{it}\ffi(x)$, one could construct a finite time blow-up solution below the minimal mass threshold, which would contradict our global well-posedness result, Theorem~\ref{global.thm}.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.label: minmass.rem

nodes.name: All minimal-mass blow-up solutions are symmetry images of one profile $S$
nodes.statement: Note that the blow-up solutions of the family exhibited in Proposition~\ref{blow-up_sol.prop} can all be retrieved from the solution \[ S(t,x) := S_{0,1,0}(t,x) = e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4t}} e^{-\frac{i}{t}} \frac{1}{|t|^{N/2}}Q\left(-\frac{x}{t}\right), \] defined on $(-\infty,0)$ and which blows up at $t=0$ with speed \[ \Vert\nabla S(t)\Vert_{L^2} \sim \frac{C}{|t|}\quad \text{as } t\uparrow0, \] for some $C>0$. Indeed, all the solutions $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ are equal to $S$, up to the symmetries (a), (b) and (c) stated in the introduction. Namely, if we apply the changes $u(t,x)\to \lambda_0^{-N/2}u(\lambda_0^{-2}t,\lambda_0^{-1}x)$, $u(t,x)\to u(t-T,x)$ and finally $u(t,x)\to e^{i\gamma_0}u(t,x)$ to $S$, we obtain $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions
nodes.statement_short: Every $S_{Q,T,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}$ is obtained from one reference solution $S$ by scaling, time-translation and phase.

nodes.name: Virial identity simplifies at $L^2$ criticality
nodes.statement: In the $L^2$ critical case, $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, (\ref{virialtwo}) reduces to \begin{equation} \Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0). \end{equation}

nodes.name: Ground states and the minimal mass $M_\mathrm{gs}$
nodes.statement: In the case $p=1+\frac{4}{N}$, we call {\em ground states} the minimizers of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$ that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}. We denote the set of ground states by $\mathcal{G}$. In view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem}~(b), there exists $M_\mathrm{gs}>0$ such that $\Vert Q\Vert_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ for all $Q\in\mathcal{G}$. We call $M_\mathrm{gs}$ the {\em minimal mass}.
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion
differentia: that are positive radial solutions of \eqref{sinls}
nodes.label: gs.def

nodes.name: The virial space $\Sigma$ and functional $\Gamma(t)$
nodes.statement: We let \[ \Sigma :=\{u \in H^1(\rn) : xu \in L^2(\rn) \}, \] and for $u(t)\in\Sigma$, we introduce \[ \Gamma(t):=\int_{\rn} |x|^2|u(t,x)|^2dx. \]

nodes.name: Proof of the minimization result and ground-state equation
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*} Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing. Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$. Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$. By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$. Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation} Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}. Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale a minimizing sequence to a fixed mass/H normalization, pass to a weak limit via symmetrization and compactness, then identify the Euler-Lagrange equation.
nodes.section: Ground states and the sharp global existence criterion

nodes.name: Proof that the pseudo-conformal transform preserves solutions
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives. For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \] It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation of the transformed derivatives and nonlinear/potential terms, substituted back into the equation.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Proof of existence of the explicit blow-up solution family
nodes.statement: The proposition is a simple consequence of Lemma~\ref{pseudo-conf.lem} applied to the global solution \[ u_{Q,\lambda_0,\gamma_0}(t,x) = e^{i\gamma_0} e^{i\lambda_0^2 t}\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0x), \] which is given by applying the scaling and phase symmetries to the standing wave $u(t,x)=e^{it}Q(x)$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the pseudo-conformal transform (Lemma pseudo-conf.lem) to the scaled, phase-rotated standing wave.
nodes.section: Construction of minimal mass blow up solutions

nodes.name: Proof of the variational characterization of ground states
nodes.statement:
It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+ rac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)\le J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer. Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial. Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization. Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \intrn  rac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \intrn  rac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \] Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert 
abla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert

Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad 	ext{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big( rac{2}{N}\Big)^{ rac{1}{2}} rac{H(|v|)^ rac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \] The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $n$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\inn$. Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $e(\overline{w}

abla(|v|)\cdot e(\overline{w}
abla w) \] and \[ \|

eq 0$ then $J^{1+ rac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+ rac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction. Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: Show $v$ (hence $|v|$) is a minimizer, that any positive minimizer is radial by symmetrization contradiction, then that $v/|v|$ is a constant phase by a second contradiction argument.

nodes.name: Proof of compactness up to translation at the minimal mass threshold
nodes.statement:
The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $n$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~ef{charact.prop}. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(n)$.} First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\Big\{ rac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})- rac{1}{p+1}\int_{n} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}= rac{1}{2}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions. Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[  egin{split} \limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\le rac{1}{2}\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) - rac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|dx \ &\le\limsup_{kightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\le 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (ef{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\ge 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad 	ext{and} \quad E(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)ightarrow 0 \quad	ext{and}\quad H(z_k)ightarrow 0. \] Hence, \[ \lim_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{kightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{n}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{n}|z_k|^{p+1}dxight)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$. Consequently, by Lemma~ef{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(n)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset n$ such that  egin{equation} \wt{v}_{n_k} ightarrow v \quad 	ext{in} \quad L^q(n), \quad  orall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \wt{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \] In particular, the sequence $\{\wt{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(n)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\wt{v}_{n_k}\wto v$ weakly in $H^1(n)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2: Localization.} We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $n$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|ightarrow\infty$ as $kightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{kightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}. We start by showing that  egin{equation} \lim_{k	o\infty} \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \intrn  rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\ge R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(n)$, there exists $C\ge0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\le R^{-2}\int_{n}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\le CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$. Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k	o\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that  egin{equation*} \liminf_{kightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R} rac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta. \end{equation*} Note that this inequality will still hold if we increase the value of $R$ or pass to a further subsequence. Let $a>0$ and $ fi\in C_0^\infty([0,\infty))$ be such that $ fi(r)=1$ for $0\le r \le R$, $ fi(r)=0$ for $r\ge R+a$, $0\le fi\le1$ and $\| fi'\|_{L^\infty}\le 1/a$. nodes.name: Proof of the sharp global well-posedness criterion
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}. By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded. We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \] Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \] Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*} It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of the classification theorem
nodes.statement:
Let $u$ be a solution of \eqref{inls} such that $\|u\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $\lim_{t\uparrow T} H(u) =+\infty$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~1.} Let $\{t_n\}_{n\in
at} \subset eal$ be a sequence of times such that $t_n\uparrow T$ as $nightarrow\infty$. We set \[ u_n=u(t_n), \quad \lambda_n^2=H(u_n), \quad v_n(x)=\lambda_n^{-N/2}u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x). \] We note that $\lambda_nightarrow\infty$ as $nightarrow\infty$, and $\|v_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_n\|_{L^2}=\|u_0\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ by the $L^2$ scaling. Furthermore, \[  egin{split} H(v_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)=1. \end{split} \] On the other hand, by conservation of the energy, \[  egin{split} E(v_n)&= rac12\lambda_n^{-2}H(u_n)- rac{1}{p+1}\lambda_n^{-2}\int_{n} |u_n(y)|^{p+1}dy\ &=\lambda_n^{-2} E(u_n)=\lambda_n^{-2}E(u_0)	o 0 \quad 	ext{as} \ n	o\infty. \end{split} \] Hence, by Proposition ef{compact.prop}, there exist $Q\in\mathcal{G}$, $\gamma_0\ineal$ and $\lambda_0>0$ such that, up to a subsequence,  egin{equation} \lim_{nightarrow\infty} \|v_n-e^{i\gamma_0}Q_{\lambda_0}\|_{H^1}=0, \end{equation} where $Q_{\lambda_0}(x)=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x)$. \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~2.} We now prove that $u_n$ concentrates all of its mass at $x=0$ as $nightarrow\infty$. We show that, in the sense of distributions, \[ |u_n|^2ightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\delta_0. \] Indeed, for any $\varphi\in C^\infty_0(n)$, using the change of variables $y=\lambda_n^{-1}x$ we find that \[  egin{split} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy &=\int_{n}|u_n(\lambda_n^{-1}x)|^2\varphi(\lambda^{-1}_nx)\lambda_n^{-N}dx =\int_{n}|v_n(x)|^2\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx\ &=\int_{n}(|v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2)\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)dx+\int_{n} |Q(x)|^2\varphi(0)dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2(\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0))dx. \end{split} \] Thus, we obtain \[  egin{split} \Big|\int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy -M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0)\Big| &\le \|\varphi\|_{L^\infty}\int_{n}||v_n(x)|^2-|Q(x)|^2|dx\ &\phantom{\le} \ +\int_{n}|Q(x)|^2|\varphi(\lambda_n^{-1}x)-\varphi(0)|dx. \end{split} \] We conclude this step by noticing that $|v_n|^2$ converges strongly to $|Q|^2$ in $L^1(n)$ from (ef{b}), so the first integral vanishes as $nightarrow\infty$. Since $\lambda_nightarrow\infty$ the second integral also converges to zero by the dominated convergence theorem. Hence, we obtain  egin{equation} \int_{n}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dyightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0). \end{equation} \medskip 
oindent {\em Step~3.} We now show that $u(t)\in\Sigma$ for all $t\in[0,T)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty_0(n)$ be a radial and non-negative function such that $\phi(x)=|x|^2$ for $|x|\le 1$. It is easy to see that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \[ |

Since the right-hand side is a positive quadratic polynomial, we must have that $|f'(r)|^2-4C'f(r)\le 0$, thus $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$, where $C=4C'>0$. abla\phi_R\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u}
abla u). \] Since $\|u\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$, we can apply Lemma ef{banica.lem} and the inequality $|
abla\phi_R|^2\le C\phi_R$, to get \[ |\Gamma'_R(t)|\le 2\sqrt{2E(u)}\Big(\int|

abla u_0) = -16E(u_0)T. \] \medskip 
oindent {\em Step 4.} We apply identity \eqref{valeria} with $u_0$, $s= rac{1}{2T}$, and $	heta(x)= rac{|x|^2}{2}$ to get \[  egin{split} E(u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}})&=E(u_0)+ rac{1}{2T}\int x\cdot	ext{Im}( ar{u_0}
abla u_0) + rac{1}{8T^2}\int|x|^2|u_0|^2\ &=E(u_0)+ rac{1}{2T}(-4E(u_0))+ rac{1}{8T^2}(8E(u_0)T^2)=0. \end{split} \] Note that this calculation justifies, {\em a posteriori}, the application of~\eqref{valeria} with $	heta(x)= rac{|x|^2}{2}
ot\in C_0^{\infty}(n)$. Since $\|u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$ and $E(u_0e^{i rac{|x|^2}{4T}})=0$, we can deduce from Proposition ef{charact.prop} that there exist $\lambda_1>0$, $\gamma_1\ineal$, and $\wt{Q}\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ u_0(x)=e^{i\gamma_1}e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\lambda_1^{N/2}\wt{Q}(\lambda_1x). \] Finally, we use the pseudo-conformal transformation. We define $	ilde\lambda_0=\lambda_1T>0$ and $	ilde\gamma_0=\gamma_1-\lambda_1^2T\ineal$, and write $u_0$ as \[ u_0(x)=e^{i	ilde\gamma_0}e^{i rac{	ilde\lambda^2_0}{T}} e^{-i rac{|x|^2}{4T}}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0}{T}\Big)^{N/2}\wt{Q}\Big( rac{	ilde\lambda_0x}{T}\Big). \] Thus, $u_0=S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}(0)$, where $S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}$ is defined by (ef{S2.def}). By invoking uniqueness of the solution of (ef{inls}), we find that $u(t)=S_{\wt{Q},T,	ilde\lambda_0,	ilde\gamma_0}(t)$ for all $t\in[0,T)$, which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale the blow-up profile near $T$, apply the compactness proposition to identify a ground state, transfer the result to $u_0$ via the virial identities and the pseudo-conformal transform.

nodes.name: $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling $u\to\m
nodes.statement: First note that the functional $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling \[ u(x) \to u^{\lambda,\mu}(x):=\mu u(\lambda x) \quad (\lambda,\mu>0). \] Indeed, we have \begin{align*} H (u^{\lambda,\mu})&=\lambda^{2-N}\mu^2 H (u),\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|_{L^2}^2&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^2\|u\|^2_{L^2},\\ \|u^{\lambda,\mu}\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}&=\lambda^{-N}\mu^{p+1}\|u\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}\\ \text{and so} \quad J^{p,N}(u^{\lambda,\mu})&=J^{p,N}(u). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $J^{p,N}$ is invariant under the scaling $u\to\mu u(\lambda\cdot)$.

nodes.name: Introduce a minimizing sequence $u_n$, then symm
nodes.statement: Let $\{u_n\}\subset H^1(\rn)$ be a minimizing sequence, $\alpha_{p,N} = \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(u_n)\ge0$. Since $J(|u|)\le J(u)$, we can suppose that $u_n\ge0$ for all $n\in\N$. Furthermore, denoting by $u_n^*$ the Schwarz symmetrization of $u_n$ (see e.g.~\cite[pp.~80-83]{Lieb}), we have that \[ \intrn \frac{(u_n^*)^{2}}{|x|^2} dx \ge \intrn \frac{u_n^{2}}{|x|^2} dx, \] \[ \Vert \nabla u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla u_n\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert u_n^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert u_n\Vert_{L^2}. \] We can therefore suppose that $u_n=u_n^*$ and, in particular, that each $u_n$ is positive, radial and radially decreasing.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce a minimizing sequence $u_n$, then symmetrize it to positive, radial, radially decreasing (Lieb-Loss).

nodes.name: Rescale the sequence to fixed mass and $H$-norm.
nodes.statement: Thanks to the scaling invariance of $J^{p,N}$, we can further rescale the minimizing sequence by choosing $\lambda_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}/H(u_n) $ and $\mu_n=\|u_n\|_{L^2}^{N/2-1}/H^{N/2}(u_n)$. We thus obtain a minimizing sequence $\psi_n=u_n^{\lambda_n,\mu_n}$ with the following properties: \begin{align*} \psi_n \ge 0, \quad \psi_n=\psi_n(|x|),\\ \|\psi_n\|_{L^2}=1, \quad H(\psi_n)=1,\\ \lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \end{align*} In particular, $\{\psi_n\}$ is bounded in $H^1(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rescale the sequence to fixed mass and $H$-norm.

nodes.name: Pass to a weak $H^1$ limit $\psi^*$, strong in $
nodes.statement: Thus, up to a subsequence, we can suppose that $\{\psi_n\}$ has a weak limit $\psi^* \in H^1(\rn)$. Since $\{\psi_n\}\subset H^1_\mathrm{rad}(\rn)$ and $p+1\in(2,2^*)$, we can also suppose that $\psi_n$ converges strongly to $\psi^*$ in $L^{p+1}(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Pass to a weak $H^1$ limit $\psi^*$, strong in $L^{p+1}$.

nodes.name: Weak lower semicontinuity pins $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi
nodes.statement: By weak lower semi-continuity of $\Vert\cdot\Vert_{L^2}$ and $H$ (see \cite{montefusco}), we obtain that $\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}\le 1$ and $H(\psi^*)\le 1$. Hence, \[ \alpha_{p,N}\le J^{p,N}(\psi^*)\le \frac{1}{\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}}=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}J^{p,N}(\psi_n)=\alpha_{p,N}. \] It follows that $H(\psi^*)^{\frac{p-1}{4}N}\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}^{2+(p-1)(2-N)/2}=1$ and, therefore, $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$.
nodes.statement_short: Weak lower semicontinuity pins $H(\psi^*)=\|\psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$.

nodes.name: Write out the Euler-Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}=
nodes.statement: Now, $\psi^*$ must satisfy the Euler--Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}(\psi^*)=0$. We first remark that, for any $u \in H^1(\rn)$, $DJ^{p,N}(u)=0$ reads \begin{equation} -N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u\Big) +\Big(1+ \frac{p-1}{4}(2-N)\Big)\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u -\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big) \frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^{p+1}}^{p+1}}|u|^{p-1}u=0. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Write out the Euler-Lagrange equation $DJ^{p,N}=0$.

nodes.name: Substitute the normalizations to recover $Q$ sol
nodes.statement: Taking into consideration $H(\psi^*)=1$, $\| \psi^*\|_{L^2}=1$, $\|\psi^*\|^{p+1}_{L^{p+1}}=\alpha_{p,N}^{-1}$ and $\psi^*\ge0$, we get \[ N\Big(\frac{p-1}{4}\Big)\Big(\Delta \psi^*+c\frac{\psi^*}{|x|^2}\Big) -\left(1+\frac{p-1}{4}(2-N) \right)\psi^*+\alpha_{p,N}\Big(\frac{p+1}{2}\Big)(\psi^*)^p=0. \] Then $Q$ defined by $\psi^*=(\alpha_{p,N}(p+1)/2)^{-1/(p-1)}Q$ readily satisfies (\ref{EL}) and \eqref{sharpestimate}.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute the normalizations to recover $Q$ solving (EL) and the sharp estimate.

nodes.name: At $p=1+4/N$, any minimizer rescales into a solu
nodes.statement: Finally, in view of Remark~\ref{gs_scaling.rem} and Remark~\ref{scaling.rem} below, if $p=1+\frac4N$ and $u$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac{4}{N},N}$, the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler} reads \begin{equation} \Delta u + \frac{c}{|x|^2} u -\frac{2}{N}\frac{H(u)}{\|u\|_{L^2}^2} u +|u|^{p-1}u=0, \end{equation} and any solution $u$ can be rescaled into a solution $Q$ of \eqref{sinls} by letting \[ u(x)=\lambda^{N/2}Q(\lambda x) \quad\text{with}\quad \lambda=\sqrt{\frac{2}{N}}\frac{\sqrt{H(u)}}{\Vert u\Vert_{L^2}}. \] The proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: At $p=1+4/N$, any minimizer rescales into a solution $Q$ of the stationary equation.

nodes.name: Take the local solution given by Theorem~\ref{lo
nodes.statement: Consider a local solution of \eqref{inls}, as given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}.
nodes.statement_short: Take the local solution given by Theorem~\ref{local.thm}.

nodes.name: Reduce, via the blow-up alternative, to showing
nodes.statement: By the blow-up alternative, we need only show that, if $\Vert u_0\Vert_{L^2}<M_\text{gs}$, then $H(u(t))$ remains bounded.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce, via the blow-up alternative, to showing $H(u(t))$ stays bounded.

nodes.name: Rewrite $H(u)$ in terms of the energy $E(u)$.
nodes.statement: We control $H(u(t))$ using the energy. By definition of $E$, \[ H(u)=2E(u) + \frac{1}{1+\frac2N}\Vert{u}\Vert_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $H(u)$ in terms of the energy $E(u)$.

nodes.name: Apply the sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg corollary to
nodes.statement: Now, by Corollary~\ref{GN.cor}, \[ \|u\|_{L^{2+\frac4N}}^{2+\frac4N}\le \left(\frac{1+\frac2N}{M_\text{gs}^{\frac4N}}\right) H(u)\|u\|_{L^2}^{\frac4N} =(1+\txt\frac2N)\disp\left(\frac{\|u\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Apply the sharp Gagliardo-Nirenberg corollary to bound $\|u\|_{L^{2+4/N}}^{2+4/N}$.

nodes.name: Use conservation of mass and energy to close the
nodes.statement: Hence, by conservation of mass and energy, \begin{align*} H(u(t)) &\le 2E(u(t))+\left(\frac{\|u(t)\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t))\\ &\phantom{\le}=2E(u_0)+\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}H(u(t)). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Use conservation of mass and energy to close the inequality.

nodes.name: Rearranging isolates $H(u(t))$, bounded uniforml
nodes.statement: It follows that \[ \left(1-\left(\frac{\|u_0\|_{L^2}}{M_\text{gs}}\right)^{\frac4N}\right)H(u(t))\le 2 E(u_0), \] which concludes the proof.
nodes.statement_short: Rearranging isolates $H(u(t))$, bounded uniformly in $t$ since $\|u_0\|_{L^2}<M_\mathrm{gs}$.

nodes.name: Differentiate $u_T$ in $t$ and compute $\Delta u
nodes.statement: Straightforward calculations give \[ \partial_t u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ \frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -i\frac{|x|^2}{4}u +\partial_t u +x\cdot\nabla u \right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] and \[ \D u_T(t,x) = \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}} \left[ -\frac{|x|^2}{4}u -i\frac{N}{2}(T-t)u -ix\cdot\nabla u +\D u\right]\! \left(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\right) \] for the derivatives.
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $u_T$ in $t$ and compute $\Delta u_T$.

nodes.name: Transform the nonlinear and potential terms.
nodes.statement: For the nonlinear term we find \[ |u_T|^{\frac{4}{N}}u_T(t,x)= \frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}|u|^{\frac{4}{N}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big), \] and for the potential term \[ c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)= c\Big|\frac{x}{T-t}\Big|^{-2}\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}u\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big). \]
nodes.statement_short: Transform the nonlinear and potential terms.

nodes.name: Summing the transformed terms recovers the equat
nodes.statement: It then follows from \eqref{inls} that \[ \begin{split} i\partial u_T(t,x)+&\Delta u_T(t,x)+c|x|^{-2}u_T(t,x)+|u_T|^{4/N}u_T(t,x) \\ &=\frac{e^{-i\frac{|x|^2}{4(T-t)}}}{(T-t)^{N/2+2}}[i\partial_tu+\Delta u+c|x|^{-2}u +|u|^{4/N}u]\Big(\frac{1}{T-t},\frac{x}{T-t}\Big)=0, \end{split} \] which proves the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Summing the transformed terms recovers the equation, equal to $0$.

nodes.name: $v$, hence $|v|$, is a minimizer of $J^{1+4/N,N}
nodes.statement: It follows directly from \eqref{valueofmin} and \eqref{varchar} that $v$ is a minimizer of $J^{1+\frac4N,N}$. Since $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)\le J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, $|v|$ is also a minimizer.
nodes.statement_short: $v$, hence $|v|$, is a minimizer of $J^{1+4/N,N}$.

nodes.name: Sub-claim: every positive minimizer is radial.
nodes.statement: Furthermore, any positive minimizer is radial.
nodes.statement_short: Sub-claim: every positive minimizer is radial.

nodes.name: Assume for contradiction a non-radial positive m
nodes.statement: Indeed, suppose $v_0$ is a positive minimizer that is not radial, and let $v_0^*$ be its Schwarz symmetrization.
nodes.statement_short: Assume for contradiction a non-radial positive minimizer $v_0$; symmetrize it.

nodes.name: Strict Hardy-term inequality under symmetrizatio
nodes.statement: Then, in view of \cite[Theorem~3.4]{Lieb}, we have that \[ \intrn \frac{|v_0^*|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx > \intrn \frac{|v_0|^{2}}{|x|^2} dx. \]
nodes.statement_short: Strict Hardy-term inequality under symmetrization (Lieb-Loss Thm 3.4).

nodes.name: Gradient/$L^2$ norms do not increase, so $J(v_0^
nodes.statement: Since, on the other hand, \[ \Vert \nabla v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le \Vert \nabla v_0\Vert_{L^2} \quad\text{and}\quad \Vert v_0^*\Vert_{L^2}\le\Vert v_0\Vert_{L^2}, \] we get $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0^*)<J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v_0)$, a contradiction. We deduce that $|v|$ is radial.
nodes.statement_short: Gradient/$L^2$ norms do not increase, so $J(v_0^*)<J(v_0)$: contradiction, hence $|v|$ radial.

nodes.name: $|v|$ solves the Euler-Lagrange equation, so $|v
nodes.statement: Now, $|v|$ satisfies the Euler--Lagrange equation \eqref{euler2} and we know there exists $Q\in\mathcal{G}$ such that \[ |v(x)|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0 x), \quad \text{where} \quad \lambda_0 =\Big(\frac{2}{N}\Big)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{H(|v|)^\frac{1}{2}}{\|v\|_{L^2}}. \]
nodes.statement_short: $|v|$ solves the Euler-Lagrange equation, so $|v|=\lambda_0^{N/2}Q(\lambda_0\cdot)$ for a ground state $Q$.

nodes.name: Reduce to showing $w=v/|v|$ is a constant phase.
nodes.statement: The proof will be complete if we show that $w(x)=v(x)/|v(x)|$ is constant on $\rn$, for this implies that there exists $\gamma_0\in\R$ such that $w(x)=e^{i\gamma_0}$ for all $x\in\rn$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to showing $w=v/|v|$ is a constant phase.

nodes.statement:
Differentiating $|w|^2=1$ yields $e(\overline{w}

nodes.statement_short: Differentiate $|w|^2=1$ to split $\|\nabla v\|_{L^2}^2$ into radial and phase-gradient parts.

nodes.name: If $\nabla w\neq 0$ then $J(|v|)<J(v)$: contradi
nodes.statement: Together with Hardy's inequality, this implies that, if $|\nabla w|\neq 0$ then $J^{1+\frac4N,N}(|v|)< J^{1+\frac4N,N}(v)$, which is a contradiction.
nodes.statement_short: If $\nabla w\neq 0$ then $J(|v|)<J(v)$: contradiction.

nodes.name: $w$ is constant, giving $v=e^{i\gamma_0}|v|$ as
nodes.statement: Hence, $w$ is constant, and the proof is complete.
nodes.statement_short: $w$ is constant, giving $v=e^{i\gamma_0}|v|$ as claimed.

nodes.name: Outline: rule out (V)/(D) to get compactness, sh
nodes.statement: The behavior of the sequence $\{v_n\}$ is constrained by the concentration-compactness lemma. Our proof proceeds in several steps: by ruling out (V) and (D), we will first show that property (C) holds in Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}. We will then prove the localization of the subsequence $\{v_{n_k}\}$, {\em i.e.}~that the sequence of translations ${y_k}$ is bounded in $\rn$. This step is the most delicate one due to the inverse-square potential, and will be handled by a subtle combination of Hardy's inequality and the Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality \eqref{GN}. Once this localization property is established, the result will follow from Proposition~\ref{charact.prop}.
nodes.statement_short: Outline: rule out (V)/(D) to get compactness, show the translations are bounded, then conclude via charact.prop.

nodes.name: Rule out vanishing and dichotomy to get compactn
nodes.statement: Step~1: Compactness in $L^q(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rule out vanishing and dichotomy to get compactness in $L^q$.

nodes.name: Vanishing (V) would force $\limsup E(v_{n_k})>0$
nodes.statement: First suppose that (V) holds. Since $p+1\in (2,2^*)$ we get, \[ \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})=\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\Big\{\frac{1}{2}H(v_{n_k})-\frac{1}{p+1}\int_{\rn} |v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx\Big\}=\frac{1}{2}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k})>0, \] which contradicts our assumptions.
nodes.statement_short: Vanishing (V) would force $\limsup E(v_{n_k})>0$: contradiction.

nodes.name: Assume dichotomy (D); properties (4)-(6) and pos
nodes.statement: Suppose now that (D) holds. Then from properties (5) and (6) it follows that \[ \begin{split} \limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\{E(w_k)+E(z_k)\}&\le\frac{1}{2}\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}H(v_{n_k}) -\frac{1}{p+1}\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\rn}|v_{n_k}|dx \\ &\le\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty} E(v_{n_k})\le 0. \end{split} \] Property (D)(4) of Lemma (\ref{conc-comp.lemma}) and inequality \eqref{posE} imply that $E(w_k), E(z_k)\ge 0$ for $k$ large enough, thus \[ E(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad \text{and} \quad E(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \] Using again property (4) and inequality \eqref{posE}, we get that \[ H(w_k)\rightarrow 0 \quad\text{and}\quad H(z_k)\rightarrow 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Assume dichotomy (D); properties (4)-(6) and posE force $E(w_k),E(z_k)\to0$ and $H(w_k),H(z_k)\to0$.

nodes.name: This forces $\int|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}\to0$, again con
nodes.statement: Hence, \[ \lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{\rn}|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}dx =\lim_{k\rightarrow\infty}\left(\int_{\rn}|w_k|^{p+1}dx+\int_{\rn}|z_k|^{p+1}dx\right)=0, \] leading again to the contradiction that $\limsup_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$.
nodes.statement_short: This forces $\int|v_{n_k}|^{p+1}\to0$, again contradicting the energy assumption: (D) is ruled out.

nodes.name: With (V),(D) excluded, the concentration-compact
nodes.statement: Consequently, by Lemma~\ref{conc-comp.lemma}, there exists $v\in H^1(\rn)$ and a sequence of translations $\{y_k\}_{k\in\N}\subset \rn$ such that \begin{equation} \wt{v}_{n_k} \rightarrow v \quad \text{in} \quad L^q(\rn), \quad \forall q\in[2,2^*), \end{equation} where we let \[ \wt{v}_{n_k}(x):=v_{n_k}(x-y_k). \]
nodes.statement_short: With (V),(D) excluded, the concentration-compactness lemma gives translated strong $L^q$ convergence.

nodes.name: The translated sequence is $L^2$-compact with ma
nodes.statement: In particular, the sequence $\{\wt{v}_{n_k}\}$ is compact in $L^2(\rn)$ and, in view of \eqref{a}, $\|v\|_{L^2}=M_\mathrm{gs}$. We shall also suppose, without loss of generality, that $\wt{v}_{n_k}\wto v$ weakly in $H^1(\rn)$.
nodes.statement_short: The translated sequence is $L^2$-compact with mass $M_\mathrm{gs}$; assume WLOG weak $H^1$ convergence too.

nodes.name: Show the translations $y_k$ are bounded, by cont
nodes.statement: Step~2: Localization.
nodes.statement_short: Show the translations $y_k$ are bounded, by contradiction.

nodes.name: Assume $|y_k|\to\infty$; aim to derive $\liminf
nodes.statement: We now prove by contradiction that the sequence of translations $\{y_k\}$ is bounded in $\rn$. Let us assume that there exists a subsequence, denoted again by $\{y_k\}$, such that $|y_k|\rightarrow\infty$ as $k\rightarrow\infty$. We will prove that, in this case, $\liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}E(v_{n_k})>0$, which contradicts \eqref{a}.
nodes.statement_short: Assume $|y_k|\to\infty$; aim to derive $\liminf E(v_{n_k})>0$.

nodes.name: Split the Hardy integral into a near-origin part
nodes.statement: We start by showing that \begin{equation} \lim_{k\to\infty} \intrn \frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = 0. \end{equation} To prove \eqref{zerolimit}, we split the integral as \[ \intrn \frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx = \underbrace{\int_{|x|<R}\frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{I}_k} +\underbrace{\int_{|x|\ge R}\frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx}_{\mathrm{II}_k}, \] for some $R>0$. We first observe that, by the boundedness of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ in $L^2(\rn)$, there exists $C\ge0$ such that \[ \mathrm{II}_k\le R^{-2}\int_{\rn}|v_{n_k}(x)|^2dx\le CR^{-2}. \] By choosing $R>0$ large, we can thus make $\mathrm{II}_k$ as small as we want, uniformly in $k$.
nodes.statement_short: Split the Hardy integral into a near-origin part $\mathrm{I}_k$ and a far part $\mathrm{II}_k\le CR^{-2}$.

nodes.name: Assume for contradiction $\mathrm{I}_k$ does not
nodes.statement: Next, we fix $R>0$ arbitrary and prove that $\lim_{k\to\infty}\mathrm{I}_k=0$. This will complete the proof of \eqref{zerolimit}. We argue by contradiction and suppose there exist $\delta>0$ and a subsequence of $\{v_{n_k}\}$ (still denoted $\{v_{n_k}\}$) such that \begin{equation*} \liminf_{k\rightarrow\infty}\int_{|x|<R}\frac{|v_{n_k}|^2}{|x|^2}dx\ge\delta. \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Assume for contradiction $\mathrm{I}_k$ does not vanish, i.e. a lower bound $\delta>0$ persists.

Since $\lambda_n\rightarrow\infty$ the second integral also converges to zero by the dominated convergence theorem. Hence, we obtain \begin{equation} \int_{\rn}|u_n(y)|^2\varphi(y)dy\rightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\varphi(0). \end{equation}

nodes.statement: Step~3.

nodes.name: Goal $u(t)\in\Sigma$; introduce a truncated weig
nodes.statement: We now show that $u(t)\in\Sigma$ for all $t\in[0,T)$. Let $\phi\in C^\infty_0(\rn)$ be a radial and non-negative function such that $\phi(x)=|x|^2$ for $|x|\le 1$. It is easy to see that there exists a constant $C>0$ such that \[ |\nabla \phi (x) |^2\le C\phi(x) \] for all $x\in\rn$.
nodes.statement_short: Goal $u(t)\in\Sigma$; introduce a truncated weight $\phi$ with $|\nabla\phi|^2\le C\phi$.

nodes.name: Taylor's formula on the radial profile $f$ of $\
nodes.statement: Indeed, since $\phi$ is radially symmetric we may choose $f\in C(\real,\real_+) $, such that $\phi(|x|)=f(|x|)$. By Taylor's formula, for all $r\in\real$ and $h\in\real$ there exists $y\in[r,r+h]$, such that \[ 0\le f(r+h)=f(r)+f'(r)h+\frac{f''(y)}{2}h^2\le f(r)+f'(r)h+C'h^2, \] where $C'=1+\max_{r\in\real}\frac{|f'(r)|}{2}>0$. Since the right-hand side is a positive quadratic polynomial, we must have that $|f'(r)|^2-4C'f(r)\le 0$, thus $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$, where $C=4C'>0$.
nodes.statement_short: Taylor's formula on the radial profile $f$ of $\phi$ proves $|f'(r)|^2\le Cf(r)$.

nodes.name: Define $\Gamma_R(t)=\int\phi_R|u|^2$ and compute
nodes.statement: For all $R>0$, we define $\phi_R(x)=R^2\phi(x/R)$, and for all $t\in[0,T)$, \[ \Gamma_R(t)=\int_{\rn}\phi_R(x)|u(t,x)|^2dx. \] A direct calculation, similar to the proof of Lemma~\ref{virial.lemma}, yields that \[ \Gamma_R'(t)=2\text{Re}\int\phi_R\bar{u}\partial_tu =-2\text{Im}\int\phi_R\bar{u}(\Delta u+\frac{c}{|x|^2}u+|u|^{p-1}u) =2\int\nabla\phi_R\cdot\text{Im}(\bar{u}\nabla u). \]
nodes.statement_short: Define $\Gamma_R(t)=\int\phi_R|u|^2$ and compute $\Gamma_R'(t)$ as in the virial lemma.

nodes.statement: Since $\|u\|_{L^2}=\|Q\|_{L^2}$, we can apply Lemma \ref{banica.lem} and the inequality $|\nabla\phi_R|^2\le C\phi_R$, to get \[ |\Gamma'_R(t)|\le 2\sqrt{2E(u)}\Big(\int|\nabla\phi_R|^2|u|^2\Big)^{1/2} \le C\sqrt{E(u_0)}\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}. \]
nodes.statement_short: Banica's lemma bounds $|\Gamma_R'(t)|\le C\sqrt{E(u_0)}\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}$.

nodes.name: Integrate the differential bound, use Step 2's c
nodes.statement: By integrating between a fixed $t\in[0,T)$ and $t_n$, we obtain, \[ |\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t)}-\sqrt{\Gamma_R(t_n)}|\le C|t-t_n|. \] Applying (\ref{c}) in Step 2, we get \[ \Gamma_R(t_n)=\int_{\rn} |u_n(x)|^2\phi_R(x)dx\rightarrow M_\mathrm{gs}^2\phi_R(0)=0. \] Thus, letting $n\to\infty$ in the last inequality, we obtain, for all $t\in [0,T)$ and all $R>0$, \[ \Gamma_R(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \] Since the right-hand side of the last expression is independent of $R$, letting $R\to\infty$ yields, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ u(t)\in\Sigma \quad\text{and}\quad 0\le \Gamma(t) \le C(T-t)^2. \]
nodes.statement_short: Integrate the differential bound, use Step 2's concentration at $t_n$, then let $n,R\to\infty$ to get $u(t)\in\Sigma$, $\Gamma(t)\le C(T-t)^2$.

Moreover, since $u(t)\in\Sigma$ and $u$ is a solution of~\eqref{inls}, we may apply Lemma~\ref{virial.lemma}, and by (\ref{virialthree}) we obtain $\Gamma''(t)=16E(u_0)$, which finally gives, for all $t\in [0,T)$, \[ \Gamma(t) = 8E(u_0)(T-t)^2. \] Letting $t=0$, we find, using identity (\ref{virialone}) \[ \Gamma(0)=\int |x|^2|u_0|^2= 8E(u_0)T^2 \quad \text{and}\quad \Gamma'(0)= 4\int x\cdot\im(\overline{u_0}\nabla u_0) = -16E(u_0)T. \]

nodes.statement: We apply identity \eqref{valeria} with $u_0$, $s=\frac{1}{2T}$, and $\theta(x)=\frac{|x|^2}{2}$ to get \[ \begin{split} E(u_0e^{i\frac{|x|^2}{4T}})&=E(u_0)+\frac{1}{2T}\int x\cdot\text{Im}(\bar{u_0}\nabla u_0) +\frac{1}{8T^2}\int|x|^2|u_0|^2\\ &=E(u_0)+\frac{1}{2T}(-4E(u_0))+\frac{1}{8T^2}(8E(u_0)T^2)=0. \end{split} \] Note that this calculation justifies, {\em a posteriori}, the application of~\eqref{valeria} with $\theta(x)=\frac{|x|^2}{2}\not\in C_0^{\infty}(\rn)$.
